definition: a roadside hotel for motorists, usually with parking beside the rooms

collocations.example: We stayed in a cheap motel near the highway.
She booked a motel room for just one night.

definition: a short phrase that expresses the beliefs or aims of a person or group

collocations.example: The school motto encourages students to work hard.
'Never give up' is our family motto.

definition: dirt, mud, or other unpleasant substance

collocations.example: His boots were covered in muck after the walk.
We had to clear the muck from the yard.

definition: a confused or disorganized state

collocations.example: All my papers are in a complete muddle.
We will get into a muddle without a plan.

definition: to attack and rob someone in a public place

collocations.example: Tourists can get mugged in crowded train stations.
She was mugged at knifepoint near the bank.

definition: involving three or more countries or parties

collocations.example: The multilateral trade talks lasted several weeks.
They signed a multilateral agreement on climate change.

definition: a large painting done directly on a wall

collocations.example: The artist was hired to paint a mural downtown.
Students painted a colorful mural on the school wall.

definition: dark and difficult to see through, especially of water

collocations.example: Fish are hard to see in the murky water.
She gazed into the murky depths of the lake.

definition: resulting from a genetic change or mutation

collocations.example: Scientists studied a mutant strain of the virus.
The mutant gene caused unusual plant growth.

definition: to damage something severely, often by cutting or tearing part of it

collocations.example: Vandals tried to mutilate the rare library book.
Vandals had mutilated the ancient statue beyond repair.

definition: the projecting nose and mouth of an animal

collocations.example: The dog pushed its wet muzzle into my hand.
She gently stroked the horse's soft muzzle.

definition: a drug that dulls the senses and is often addictive

collocations.example: Doctors prescribed a powerful narcotic to ease the pain.
Police seized a large shipment of illegal narcotics.

definition: relating to the nose

collocations.example: The doctor recommended a nasal spray for his allergies.
Nasal congestion makes it hard to breathe at night.

definition: lacking money or basic necessities; very poor

collocations.example: The charity provides food for needy families every winter.
Donations will help needy children attend school.

definition: to make something ineffective or cancel out its effect

collocations.example: High costs could negate the benefits of the plan.
One mistake can negate the effect of hard work.

definition: so small or unimportant that it can be ignored

collocations.example: The price increase had a negligible effect on sales.
The project added only a negligible amount of cost.

definition: bright, colorful lighting used in signs, produced by glowing gas

collocations.example: A neon sign flashed above the bar entrance.
The city streets glowed with bright neon lights.

definition: to settle comfortably and snugly against someone or something

collocations.example: The child nestled against her mother's shoulder.
The kitten nestled into the warm blanket.

definition: relating to nerves or the nervous system

collocations.example: Neural networks mimic how the human brain works.
The drug affects neural activity in the brain.

definition: the branch of medicine dealing with nerves and the nervous system

collocations.example: She trained in neurology at a famous hospital.
The neurology department treats patients with brain disorders.

definition: to take small, gentle bites of something

collocations.example: The birds nibble at the seeds on the ground.
She nibbled on a biscuit during the meeting.

definition: to bite or pinch someone or something sharply and quickly

collocations.example: The small dog tried to nip at my ankles.
The crab can nip your finger with its claws.

definition: a person who moves from place to place rather than living in one spot

collocations.example: Desert nomads travel with their herds across the sand.
As a digital nomad, she works from different countries.

definition: relating to standards or rules of what should be done

collocations.example: The study used normative standards to judge behavior.
Normative analyzis asks what policies ought to be.

definition: feeling a fond longing for a happier time in the past

collocations.example: Old songs make me feel nostalgic about college.
The photos brought back nostalgic memories of childhood.

definition: the act of formally informing someone, or a message that does this

collocations.example: Please give advance notification if you cannot attend.
We received notification of the schedule changes yesterday.

definition: a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea

collocations.example: A proper noun always begins with a capital letter.
Add an 's' to form most plural nouns.

definition: a very small difference in meaning, feeling, or expression

collocations.example: He noticed the subtle nuance in her tone.
A good translation should capture every nuance of meaning.

definition: a fertile place in a desert where water is found

collocations.example: The travelers rested at a desert oasis with palm trees.
Camels drank at the small oasis before continuing.

definition: a cereal grain eaten as food or fed to animals

collocations.example: She eats a bowl of oats every morning.
Rolled oats are the main ingredient in the recipe.

definition: a published notice of someone's death, often with a short life story

collocations.example: The newspaper published a long obituary for the author.
She was asked to write his obituary for the paper.

definition: to destroy something completely, leaving no trace

collocations.example: A single bomb could obliterate the whole city.
Time had obliterated all trace of the ancient village.

definition: not aware of what is happening around one

collocations.example: She was completely oblivious to the danger ahead.
He walked on, oblivious to the noise around him.

definition: no longer used or useful because something newer has replaced it

collocations.example: New technology made the old machines obsolete.
The factory replaced all its obsolete equipment.

definition: to flow out slowly and steadily

collocations.example: Blood began to ooze from the small wound.
Thick lava oozed slowly out of the crater.

definition: not able to be seen through; not transparent

collocations.example: They installed opaque glass for extra privacy.
The chemicals turned the clear liquid opaque.

definition: most favorable or best for a particular purpose

collocations.example: The plants grow best under optimum conditions.
Regular servicing keeps the engine at optimum performance.

definition: to arrange or direct something carefully to achieve an effect

collocations.example: He helped orchestrate a campaign to win votes.
The protest was carefully orchestrated by local activists.

definition: a plant with showy, often fragrant flowers

collocations.example: She grows a rare orchid in her greenhouse.
We found a wild orchid blooming in the forest.

definition: to officially make someone a priest or religious minister

collocations.example: The bishop will ordain three new priests this Sunday.
She was ordained as a minister last year.

definition: elaborately or heavily decorated

collocations.example: The palace had ornate carvings on every wall.
She admired the ornate decoration of the ceiling.

definition: a belief or practice that is widely accepted as correct

collocations.example: These ideas became the new orthodoxy among economists.
Young scientists often challenge the prevailing orthodoxy.

definition: a sudden, strong expression of emotion

collocations.example: Everyone was shocked by his sudden angry outburst.
She apologised later for her emotional outburst.

definition: to be greater in number than another group

collocations.example: In this office, women greatly outnumber men.
The enemy soldiers outnumbered us by three to one.

definition: a patient who receives treatment without staying overnight in hospital

collocations.example: He visited the outpatient clinic for a check-up.
The surgery was done, and she was treated as an outpatient.

definition: expressing opinions openly and frankly, even when they may upset people

collocations.example: She is an outspoken critic of the new law.
He became an outspoken supporter of the reforms.

definition: extended or reached out as far as possible

collocations.example: She ran toward him with outstretched arms.
He greeted each guest with an outstretched hand.

definition: too large an amount of a drug taken at one time

collocations.example: He was rushed to hospital after a drug overdose.
She nearly died after taking an overdose of pills.

definition: not done or paid by the expected or required time

collocations.example: The company charged a fee for the overdue payment.
These reforms are long overdue in our country.

definition: a part of something that sticks out above the part below

collocations.example: They sheltered under a rock overhang during the storm.
The roof overhang protects the walls from rain.

definition: a layer of something placed on top of another thing

collocations.example: A transparent overlay highlights the key areas.
The app uses a map overlay to show traffic.

definition: too great an amount or load to handle

collocations.example: Many employees complain of work overload these days.
Too many emails can cause information overload.

definition: to defeat or control someone by greater strength

collocations.example: It took three guards to overpower the attacker.
The larger team easily overpowered their opponents.

definition: to spread over or occupy a place in large numbers

collocations.example: The old house was overrun with mice and rats.
Enemy soldiers quickly overran the small town.

definition: to make something seem less important or impressive

collocations.example: The scandal overshadowed all his earlier achievements.
Her talent completely overshadowed the other performers.

definition: the act of watching over and supervising something

collocations.example: The committee provides oversight of government spending.
Stronger oversight is needed to prevent future fraud.

definition: an elaborate public show or procession, often celebrating history

collocations.example: The town staged a colorful historical pageant each summer.
Thousands watched the colorful pageant wind through the streets.

definition: done with great care, effort, and attention to detail

collocations.example: The discovery came after years of painstaking research.
He restored the old painting with painstaking care.

definition: a single sheet of glass in a window or door

collocations.example: A ball broke the window pane in the kitchen.
Rain streamed down the cold glass pane.

definition: a wide, unbroken view of a large area

collocations.example: The tower offers a stunning panorama of the city.
From the hill, we enjoyed a panorama of the valley.

definition: a large wild cat, especially a black leopard

collocations.example: A black panther moved silently through the jungle.
The scientists tracked a panther and its cubs.

definition: organized like a military force but not part of the official army

collocations.example: A paramilitary force guarded the border crossing.
Police arrested members of a violent paramilitary group.

definition: unreasonably anxious that others are trying to harm you

collocations.example: He grew paranoid that his colleagues were plotting against him.
Don't get paranoid; nobody is following you.

definition: a member of a local church community

collocations.example: The priest visited an elderly parishioner in hospital.
Local parishioners gathered for the Sunday service.

definition: the state of being equal, especially in pay or status

collocations.example: Workers are demanding pay parity with their colleagues.
Women have yet to achieve parity in many fields.

definition: the early release of a prisoner on condition of good behavior

collocations.example: He was released from prison on parole last month.
Her parole hearing is scheduled for next week.

definition: a secret word or phrase used to gain access to something

collocations.example: You must enter a password to access the system.
Remember to change your password every few months.

definition: coming from the father's side of the family

collocations.example: His paternal grandfather came from a small village.
The disease is passed down through the paternal line.

definition: decayed plant material from bogs, used as fuel or for gardening

collocations.example: The farmers cut peat from the bog for fuel.
They used to burn peat to heat their homes.

definition: to strike or pick at something with the beak

collocations.example: The hens peck at the grain in the yard.
A small bird began to peck the ground for seeds.

definition: a quick or secret look at something

collocations.example: She took a quick peek inside the box.
The company gave fans a sneak peek of the film.

definition: to look quickly or secretly at something

collocations.example: The children peeped at the puppies through the fence.
She peeped through the curtains to see outside.

definition: a small, hard, rounded piece of a substance

collocations.example: The stove burns wood pellets to produce heat.
The machine pressed the powder into a small pellet.

definition: the large bony structure at the base of the spine

collocations.example: He fractured his pelvis in the car accident.
The human pelvis supports the weight of the body.

definition: relating to the punishment of criminals under the law

collocations.example: The new penal code increased sentences for theft.
Reforms to the penal system were long overdue.

definition: to punish someone or put them at a disadvantage

collocations.example: The rules should not penalise honest taxpayers unfairly.
The referee can penalise players for dangerous tackles.

definition: able to be noticed or sensed

collocations.example: Her foreign accent was barely perceptible to me.
There was no perceptible difference between the two samples.

definition: relating to the way the senses take in information

collocations.example: Some children develop perceptual skills earlier than others.
The drug can change a person's perceptual experience.

definition: to spread throughout every part of something

collocations.example: The smell of coffee permeated through the whole house.
The scent of roses permeated the whole garden.

definition: to confuse or puzzle someone

collocations.example: The strange results continue to perplex scientists.
Her sudden silence deeply perplexed everyone present.

definition: to keep trying to do something despite difficulty

collocations.example: You must persevere with difficult students and stay patient.
She persevered in her studies despite many setbacks.

definition: the image or character that someone presents to other people

collocations.example: His public persona differs from his private self.
The singer adopted a bold stage persona.

definition: to make something suit a particular person's needs or tastes

collocations.example: You can personalise the message with your own photo.
The shop lets customers personalise their orders online.

definition: directly relevant to the matter being considered

collocations.example: She asked several pertinent questions during the meeting.
Please include all pertinent information in your report.

definition: to change something from its proper or intended use or meaning

collocations.example: They were accused of trying to pervert the course of justice.
The article perverts the truth to mislead readers.

definition: tending to expect the worst to happen

collocations.example: She feels pessimistic about her chances of promotion.
The report takes a deeply pessimistic view of the economy.

definition: a long wooden bench for seating in a church

collocations.example: The old wooden pews filled the small church.
They sat in the front pew during the service.

definition: a ghost or something that appears real but is not

collocations.example: Sailors claimed to see a ghostly phantom at sea.
A pale phantom figure seemed to drift down the hall.

definition: remarkable or extraordinary in amount or quality

collocations.example: The product has been a phenomenal success worldwide.
The company reported phenomenal growth this year.

definition: not genuine or real; fake

collocations.example: He gave a phony excuse for being late.
The salesman greeted us with a phony smile.

definition: a chemical compound containing phosphorus, often used in fertilizers

collocations.example: Farmers add phosphate fertilizer to improve the soil.
Bones contain large amounts of calcium phosphate.

definition: a copy of a document made by a photocopying machine

collocations.example: Please make a photocopy of your passport.
He showed me a clear photocopy of the contract.

definition: a tiny particle of light or other electromagnetic energy

collocations.example: The energy of a photon depends on its frequency.
The detector can register even a single photon.

definition: the scientific study of how living things function

collocations.example: The course covers both anatomy and human physiology.
Her research focuses on the physiology of desert plants.

definition: expressed or shown using pictures

collocations.example: The book gives a pictorial representation of the process.
They kept a pictorial record of the expedition.
